newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: KNP Leykam says 96 net loss of 496 mln ats.
newsitem.headline: KNP Leykam says 96 net loss of 496 mln ats.

text.p: Austria's papermaker KNP Leykam, majority owned by Dutch KNP BT, reported a net loss on Thursday of 496 million schillings in 1996, compared to a profit of 2.16 billion schillings in 1995.
The company said it would not pay any dividend in 1996.
In a statement KNP Leykam, 69.5 percent owned by KNP BT and 30.5 percent by Austria's Leykam-Muerztaler, said it was unable to recoup first half operating losses despite good capacity utilisation.

Turnover fell 33 percent to 13.73 billion schillings, mainly following the sale at the end of 1995 of its Bruck plant and paper wholesale activities. Paper prices that were on average 10-20 percent down on the previous year also contributed to the lower turnover.
KNP Leykam said it would continue its drive to cut costs in 1997. It has already announced 500 job losses at its Austrian plant.
The firm would also continue to seek a partner in the industry. It said it had already held a series of talks but gave no further details.
KNP BT owns a 72 percent stake in Leykam-Muerztaler.
